subject: evs
prompt_en: Two children at a signal: Aman crosses when the cars' light turns red and the green walking figure lights up. Bela crosses when the cars' light turns green. Who is right, and why?
prompt_hi: Signal pe do bachche: Aman tab paar karta hai jab gaadiyon ki batti laal hoti hai aur hara chalta hua aadmi jalta hai. Bela tab paar karti hai jab gaadiyon ki batti hari hoti hai. Kaun sahi hai, aur kyon?
answer: Aman. When the cars' light is red the cars stop, and the green walking figure shows it is safe for people. Bela is crossing just as the cars start moving, which is dangerous.

subject: evs
prompt_en: There is no footpath on the road to your tuition class. Which side of the road should you walk on, and why?
prompt_hi: Tumhari tuition class ke raaste mein footpath nahi hai. Sadak ke kis taraf chalna chahiye, aur kyon?
answer: On the right edge of the road, facing the oncoming traffic, so you can see vehicles coming towards you and step aside; walk in single file.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Your family visits a crowded mela with many roads around it, and you are holding your little cousin's hand. Make a safety plan for crossing roads and staying together.
prompt_hi: Tumhari family ek bheed wale mele mein jaati hai jiske aas-paas kai sadakein hain, aur tumne apne chhote cousin ka haath pakda hai. Sadak paar karne aur saath rehne ka safety plan banao.
answer: Hold hands all the time; agree on a meeting point if anyone gets separated; cross only at crossings or with an adult; stop and look right, left and right again; walk, don't run; know a parent's phone number; if lost, go to a police person or a uniformed helper.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Draw a road near a school with a zebra crossing, a traffic signal and a footpath. Draw a child crossing safely, and mark with arrows where the child looks first, second and third.
prompt_hi: School ke paas ki ek sadak banao jismein zebra crossing, traffic signal aur footpath ho. Ek bachche ko surakshit sadak paar karte hue banao, aur teer se dikhao ki woh pehle, doosre aur teesre kahaan dekhta hai.
answer: The child stands at the footpath edge at the zebra crossing; arrow 1 points right, arrow 2 left, arrow 3 right again; the walking figure is green and the child crosses in a straight line.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Rahul says, 'The safest way to cross a busy road is to run really fast, zig-zagging between the cars.' What's wrong?
prompt_hi: Rahul kehta hai, 'Bheed wali sadak paar karne ka sabse surakshit tareeka hai bahut tez bhaagna, gaadiyon ke beech zig-zag karte hue.' Galti kya hai?
answer: Running and zig-zagging can make you trip or pop up suddenly in front of a driver who cannot stop in time. Cross at a zebra crossing, walk briskly in a straight line and keep looking.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Teach your younger sibling the steps to cross a road safely on the way to school.
prompt_hi: Apne chhote bhai ya behen ko school jaate waqt surakshit sadak paar karne ke steps sikhao.
answer: Find a zebra crossing, overbridge or signal; stop at the edge; look right, left and right again and listen; cross when it is clear or the walking figure is green; walk straight without running and keep looking; never cross from behind a parked vehicle.

subject: evs
prompt_en: From last time: in which order do we look before crossing a road in India?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: India mein sadak paar karne se pehle kis kram mein dekhte hain?
answer: Right, then left, then right again.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Match each dance to its state. Dances: Bharatanatyam, Bhangra, Bihu, Garba. States: Assam, Gujarat, Punjab, Tamil Nadu.
prompt_hi: Har nritya ko uske rajya se milao. Nritya: Bharatanatyam, Bhangra, Bihu, Garba. Rajya: Assam, Gujarat, Punjab, Tamil Nadu.
answer: Bharatanatyam: Tamil Nadu. Bhangra: Punjab. Bihu: Assam. Garba: Gujarat.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Name the classical music tradition of north India and the one of south India.
prompt_hi: Uttar Bharat ki shastriya sangeet parampara aur Dakshin Bharat ki parampara ka naam batao.
answer: Hindustani music in the north and Carnatic music in the south.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Guess first: out of every 10 people in India, how many have Hindi as their mother tongue: all 10, about 8, or about 4?
prompt_hi: Pehle guess karo: India ke har 10 logon mein se kitno ki maatrubhaasha Hindi hai: saare 10, lagbhag 8, ya lagbhag 4?
answer: About 4 out of 10, a little less than half. Most Indians have another language as their mother tongue, although many also understand Hindi.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Predict: does a rupee note show its value in just one or two languages, or in many? Then look at the back of a note and count the languages in the small panel.
prompt_hi: Guess karo: rupaye ke note pe uski keemat sirf ek-do bhaashaon mein likhi hoti hai, ya bahut saari bhaashaon mein? Phir note ke peeche ki chhoti patti dekh ke bhaashayein gino.
answer: Many. The language panel on the back shows the amount in 15 Indian languages, and Hindi and English appear on the note as well.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Why do many Indians speak two or three languages?
prompt_hi: Bahut saare Indians do ya 3 bhaashayein kyon bolte hain?
answer: They speak their home language, use the state's language or Hindi with neighbours, and learn English or Hindi at school or work; people moving between states and living together makes this useful.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Compare Kathakali from Kerala with Bhangra from Punjab. How are they different, and what do they share?
prompt_hi: Kerala ke Kathakali aur Punjab ke Bhangra ki tulna karo. Dono mein kya farak hai, aur kya ek jaisa hai?
answer: Kathakali is a classical dance-drama with elaborate face make-up and costumes that tells stories through expressions and hand gestures, with drums. Bhangra is an energetic folk dance often linked with the harvest, danced to the dhol. Both use music and rhythm, celebrate or tell something, and are part of India's culture.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Think of your class or colony. Ask three friends what language they speak at home. How many different languages did you find?
prompt_hi: Apni class ya colony ke baare mein socho. 3 doston se poochho ki woh ghar pe kaunsi bhaasha bolte hain. Kitni alag bhaashayein mili?
answer: Answers vary; usually more than one language turns up even in one class or colony, which shows India's variety close to home.

subject: evs
prompt_en: A family from Assam moves to Pune. Name two ways they and their new neighbours could share and enjoy each other's culture.
prompt_hi: Assam ki ek family Pune shift hoti hai. Do tareeke batao jinse woh aur unke naye padosi ek doosre ki sanskriti baant aur enjoy kar sakein.
answer: Any two: share food such as Assamese pitha and Maharashtrian puran poli, invite each other to their festivals, learn a few words of Assamese and Marathi, teach each other dances like Bihu or Lavani, or songs.

subject: evs
prompt_en: On an outline map of India, place these dances: Bihu, Garba, Bharatanatyam, Bhangra, Kathakali, Odissi. Tell me which part of India each is from.
prompt_hi: India ke khaali map pe ye nritya lagao: Bihu, Garba, Bharatanatyam, Bhangra, Kathakali, Odissi. Batao har ek India ke kis hisse se hai.
answer: Bihu: Assam, north-east. Garba: Gujarat, west. Bharatanatyam: Tamil Nadu, south. Bhangra: Punjab, north. Kathakali: Kerala, south-west. Odissi: Odisha, east.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Golu says, 'Hindi is India's only language; everyone everywhere speaks it at home.' What's wrong?
prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai, 'Hindi India ki ikloti bhaasha hai; har jagah sab log ghar pe yahi bolte hain.' Galti kya hai?
answer: India has many languages: the Constitution lists 22 and hundreds more are spoken. Most Indians speak a different language at home, such as Tamil, Bengali, Marathi or Telugu, though many also understand Hindi.

subject: evs
prompt_en: A child from another country asks you, 'What is India like?' Tell her about India's languages, music and dances in a way that shows how varied it is.
prompt_hi: Doosre desh ka ek bachcha tumse poochhta hai, 'India kaisa hai?' Use India ki bhaashaon, sangeet aur nrityon ke baare mein aise batao ki pata chale India kitna rang-birangi hai.
answer: Many languages (22 in the Constitution, hundreds spoken; Hindi is the most spoken but most people have another mother tongue); dances such as Bharatanatyam, Kathakali, Odissi, Bihu, Garba and Bhangra; Hindustani and Carnatic music; food changes by region; people share and respect each other's cultures.

subject: evs
prompt_en: From last time: Garba is a dance from which state?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: Garba kis rajya ka nritya hai?
answer: Gujarat.

subject: evs
prompt_en: What are the three colours of our national flag from top to bottom, and what is in the middle?
prompt_hi: Hamare rashtriya dhwaj ke 3 rang upar se neeche kaunse hain, aur beech mein kya hai?
answer: Saffron at the top, white in the middle with a navy-blue Ashoka Chakra, and green at the bottom.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Who wrote our national anthem 'Jana Gana Mana', and who wrote our national song 'Vande Mataram'?
prompt_hi: Hamara rashtriya gaan 'Jana Gana Mana' kisne likha, aur rashtriya geet 'Vande Mataram' kisne likha?
answer: Rabindranath Tagore wrote 'Jana Gana Mana'; Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay wrote 'Vande Mataram'.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Before counting, guess: how many spokes does the Ashoka Chakra on our flag have: 12, 24 or 32? Then look closely at a flag or a picture and count.
prompt_hi: Ginne se pehle guess karo: hamare jhande ke Ashoka Chakra mein kitni teeliyaan hain: 12, 24 ya 32? Phir jhande ya photo ko dhyaan se dekh ke gino.
answer: 24 spokes.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Look at the emblem on a coin or a rupee note and count the lions you can see. Now predict: how many lions were carved on the real Lion Capital of Ashoka at Sarnath?
prompt_hi: Kisi sikke ya note pe bane emblem mein dikhne waale sher gino. Ab guess karo: Sarnath ke asli Ashoka stambh (Lion Capital) pe kitne sher bane the?
answer: Four lions sitting back to back. A flat picture shows only three because the fourth is hidden behind.

subject: evs
prompt_en: What do the saffron, white and green bands and the Ashoka Chakra on our flag stand for?
prompt_hi: Hamare jhande ki kesariya, safed aur hari patti aur Ashoka Chakra kis baat ke prateek hain?
answer: Saffron: courage and strength. White: peace and truth. Green: growth and the fertile land. The Ashoka Chakra: the wheel of law and moving forward.

subject: evs
prompt_en: How is Independence Day (15 August) different from Republic Day (26 January)?
prompt_hi: Swatantrata Diwas (15 August) aur Ganatantra Diwas (26 January) mein kya farak hai?
answer: On 15 August 1947 India became free from British rule. On 26 January 1950 India's Constitution came into force and India became a republic that chooses its own leaders.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Find the national emblem on something at home: a coin, a rupee note or a government letter. What words are written under the emblem, and what do they mean? (If you can't find them, look at a picture of the emblem.)
prompt_hi: Ghar pe kisi cheez pe rashtriya emblem dhoondho: sikka, note ya sarkari chitthi. Emblem ke neeche kya likha hai, aur uska matlab kya hai? (Na mile toh emblem ki photo dekho.)
answer: 'Satyameva Jayate', written in Devanagari script; it means 'Truth alone triumphs'.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Your class needs a class monitor. Should the teacher pick the child whose elder sibling was monitor last year, or should the class vote? How is this like India being a republic?
prompt_hi: Class ko monitor chahiye. Kya teacher us bachche ko chune jiska bada bhai ya behen pichhle saal monitor tha, ya class vote kare? Ye India ke ganrajya hone jaisa kaise hai?
answer: The class should vote. In a republic, the people choose their leaders by voting; the job does not pass down in a family the way a king's throne does.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Draw and colour the national flag correctly, and label what each colour and the chakra stand for.
prompt_hi: Rashtriya dhwaj sahi tareeke se banao aur rang bharo, aur label karo ki har rang aur chakra kis baat ka prateek hai.
answer: Three equal horizontal bands: saffron on top, white in the middle with a navy-blue 24-spoke chakra, green at the bottom; labels: courage and strength, peace and truth, growth and fertile land, wheel of law.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Chintu says, 'Our national animal is the lion; that's why there are lions on the emblem!' What's the mix-up?
prompt_hi: Chintu kehta hai, 'Hamara rashtriya pashu sher (lion) hai, isliye emblem pe sher bane hain!' Gadbad kahaan hai?
answer: The national animal is the tiger. The lions on the emblem come from the Lion Capital of Ashoka at Sarnath; they are part of the emblem, not the national animal.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Explain to a younger child what we celebrate on Republic Day, and name three national symbols with what they mean.
prompt_hi: Ek chhote bachche ko samjhao ki Republic Day pe hum kya manaate hain, aur 3 rashtriya prateek unke matlab ke saath batao.
answer: On 26 January 1950 India's Constitution came into force and India became a republic where people choose their leaders. Symbols: the flag (courage, peace, growth, wheel of law), the emblem (Satyameva Jayate, truth alone triumphs), the tiger, the peacock, the lotus, the anthem.

subject: evs
prompt_en: From last time: what is India's national tree, and what is our national aquatic animal?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: India ka rashtriya vriksh kaunsa hai, aur rashtriya jaliya jeev kaunsa hai?
answer: The banyan tree and the Ganges river dolphin.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Where are the Western Ghats? Name two animals that live there.
prompt_hi: Western Ghats kahaan hain? Wahaan rehne waale do jaanwar batao.
answer: A long chain of hills running along India's west coast, from Gujarat down through Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka and Kerala to Tamil Nadu. Animals: any two of the lion-tailed macaque, Nilgiri tahr, Malabar giant squirrel, great hornbill, king cobra, tiger, elephant.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Ask an adult to put a brick, or a stone about the size of your fist, into a bucket with a little water so its top sticks out above the water: a model island. Predict: if you push the top gently, will it float away like a boat? What is holding it up?
prompt_hi: Kisi bade se kaho ki ek eent, ya mutthi jitna patthar, thode paani wali baalti mein aise rakhein ki uska upar wala hissa paani ke bahar dikhe: ye hua model dweep. Guess karo: upar se halka dhakka doge toh kya ye naav ki tarah tair ke chala jayega? Ise kaun sambhaal raha hai?
answer: No, it stays where it is, because it rests on the bottom of the bucket. Real islands are the tops of land or mountains rising from the sea floor; they do not float.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Moist monsoon winds from the Arabian Sea blow towards the Western Ghats and have to rise over them. Predict: which side of the Ghats gets more rain, the side facing the sea or the far side?
prompt_hi: Arabian Sea se nami bhari monsoon hawa Western Ghats ki taraf aati hai aur use unke upar chadhna padta hai. Guess karo: Ghats ke kis taraf zyada baarish hogi, samudra wali taraf ya doosri taraf?
answer: The side facing the sea, the west. As the air rises it cools and drops most of its water as rain; the far, eastern side gets much less rain.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Corals are living animals that need clean, not-too-warm sea water. Predict: what might happen to a coral reef if the sea around it stays too warm for many weeks?
prompt_hi: Coral jeevit jaanwar hain jinhe saaf aur bahut zyada garam na ho aisa samudri paani chahiye. Guess karo: agar reef ke aas-paas samudra kai hafton tak bahut garam rahe toh kya ho sakta hai?
answer: The corals get stressed and lose the tiny colourful algae living inside them, so they turn white (coral bleaching); if the heat lasts too long they can die, and the fish that depend on them lose their home.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Why do the Western Ghats have such thick, green forests full of different animals?
prompt_hi: Western Ghats mein itne ghane, hare jungle aur itne tarah ke jaanwar kyon hain?
answer: They get very heavy monsoon rain and stay warm, so plants grow thickly; many kinds of animals find food and shelter there, and some are found nowhere else.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Why are coral reefs called the 'rainforests of the sea'?
prompt_hi: Coral reef ko 'samudra ke rainforest' kyon kaha jaata hai?
answer: Like rainforests, they are home to a huge variety of living things: fish, crabs, turtles and many others find food and shelter among the corals.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Compare the Andaman Islands with the Thar Desert. Think about water, plants and animals.
prompt_hi: Andaman dweepon aur Thar registan ki tulna karo. Paani, paudhon aur jaanwaron ke baare mein socho.
answer: The Andamans have sea all around, lots of rain, thick green forests, coral reefs and many animals. The Thar gets little rain, is sandy, and has fewer plants such as khejri and thorny bushes, with animals like camels and the desert fox that cope with dryness. Each place's life suits its conditions.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Mumbai is on the side of the Western Ghats facing the sea; Pune is on the far side. Which city do you think gets more monsoon rain?
prompt_hi: Mumbai Western Ghats ki samudra wali taraf hai; Pune doosri taraf. Tumhare hisaab se kis shehar mein zyada monsoon baarish hoti hai?
answer: Mumbai. It gets far more rain than Pune, because Pune lies on the far side of the Ghats, which the rain clouds have mostly emptied themselves on.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Mawsynram and Cherrapunji in Meghalaya are among the wettest places on Earth. They sit on hills facing moist winds from the Bay of Bengal. Use what you learned about the Western Ghats to explain why they get so much rain.
prompt_hi: Meghalaya ke Mawsynram aur Cherrapunji duniya ki sabse zyada baarish wali jagahon mein hain. Ye Bay of Bengal se aati nami bhari hawa ke saamne pahadon pe base hain. Western Ghats se jo seekha, uske hisaab se samjhao inhe itni baarish kyon milti hai.
answer: Moist winds from the Bay of Bengal are pushed up the Khasi hills, cool as they rise, and drop huge amounts of rain on the side facing the winds, just like the sea-facing side of the Western Ghats.
